study.comparator: insulin detemir titrated once or twice daily to a fasting glucose target
study.notes: STUDY: 30 week (4 week screening, 26 week intervention) phase 3 multicentre randomised open label parallel active comparator trial, NCT01003184 / H8O-EW-GWDL, exenatide 2 mg once weekly against insulin detemir titrated once or twice daily to a fasting glucose target below 5.5 mmol/L, both added to continuing metformin with or without a sulfonylurea, in type 2 diabetes with HbA1c 7.1 to 10.0 per cent and BMI 25 to 45; 222 randomised, 216 in the full analysis set (111 and 105), 191 completed. Randomisation was central, computer generated and stratified by baseline HbA1c band and sulfonylurea use. SOURCE: every number here is the sponsor's posted registry result, read on 16 October into work/fulltext/companion/nct01003184_eqw_vs_detemir_registry_results.txt, because the Europe PMC full text of Davies 2013 carries the narrative but not Table 1: the publisher renders that table as a graphic whose enlarged view is behind a subscriber gate, and the agent does not sign in. One analysis set and one dispersion convention therefore apply to all six rows (least squares mean with its standard error per arm, route arm_sems, with the per outcome analysed n on each row). The article's intention to treat HbA1c figures differ from the registry's by 0.02 percentage points (article minus 1.30 (0.08) against minus 0.88 (0.08); registry minus 1.32 (0.076) against minus 0.91 (0.077) on 95 and 96 patients), which is recorded rather than reconciled. DENOMINATORS: the registry posts a baseline only for HbA1c (8.4 (0.85) and 8.4 (0.88) per cent) and weight (96.7 (17.03) and 97.9 (15.82) kg), so the HbA1c row converts to the percent scale while fasting glucose, both pressures, total cholesterol and triglycerides carry no denominator and stay on the absolute scale until the Table 1 baselines are obtained. NOT EXTRACTED, because the article holds them only inside the table graphic: high sensitivity C reactive protein (analysed on the log scale with values of 10 mg/L or more excluded and reported as a geometric least squares mean ratio, with the text stating exenatide was significantly better than detemir, P < 0.004), adiponectin, plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 (P < 0.006), heart rate, BMI, waist circumference and LDL cholesterol. That is the single most valuable missing capture of this group: hsCRP and adiponectin for 216 patients. pct_weight_change minus 3.77 computed by the session: the two arm weight changes are minus 2.79 and plus 0.88 kg, a difference of minus 3.67 kg over the total baseline weight of 97.3 kg, 100*(-3.67)/97.3 = -3.77. industry_funded TRUE: sponsored by AstraZeneca with Eli Lilly and Company as collaborator, and the article states the study was supported by Amylin Pharmaceuticals and Eli Lilly

rows.notes: Registry outcome 3, change in HbA1c to week 26, least squares mean (SE) minus 1.32 (0.076) exenatide against minus 0.91 (0.077) detemir, mixed models, n 95 and 96; baseline 8.4 (0.85) and 8.4 (0.88) per cent from the registry baseline section. The article prints minus 1.30 (0.08) against minus 0.88 (0.08) on the full analysis set

Registry outcome 8, change in fasting serum glucose to week 26, least squares mean (SE) minus 2.33 (0.191) against minus 2.43 (0.196) mmol/L, ANCOVA with last observation carried forward, n 108 and 104; no baseline fasting glucose is posted and the article's is inside the Table 1 graphic, so this row has no percent scale denominator. The article's arm figures are minus 2.3 (95 per cent CI minus 2.7 to minus 2.0) and minus 2.4 (minus 2.8 to minus 2.1) with no significant difference

Registry outcome 9, change in systolic pressure to week 26, least squares mean (SE) minus 7.37 (1.342) against minus 2.65 (1.339) mmHg, mixed models, n 95 and 98; the article reports the between arm difference as significant (P < 0.01). No baseline pressure is posted, so the row has no percent scale denominator

Registry outcome 10, change in diastolic pressure to week 26, least squares mean (SE) minus 0.79 (0.855) against minus 0.34 (0.859) mmHg, mixed models, n 95 and 98. No baseline pressure is posted, so the row has no percent scale denominator

Registry outcome 11, change in total cholesterol to week 26, least squares mean (SE) minus 0.09 (0.067) against plus 0.06 (0.068) mmol/L, ANCOVA with last observation carried forward, n 105 and 100; the article states the between treatment lipid differences were not significant. No baseline is posted, so the row has no percent scale denominator

Registry outcome 13, change in triglycerides to week 26, least squares mean (SE) minus 0.01 (0.079) against minus 0.08 (0.081) mmol/L, ANCOVA with last observation carried forward, n 105 and 100. No baseline is posted, so the row has no percent scale denominator

json.design: randomised open label parallel active comparator phase 3, 26 weeks on treatment
other_markers: Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite
tables_used: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01003184 posted results, baseline characteristics and outcome measures 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 13 (companion capture)

rob.justification: d1 low: central computer generated randomisation through an interactive voice response system, stratified by baseline HbA1c band and sulfonylurea use. d2 high: open label, a weekly injection against a titrated daily insulin, and the article states that forced titration of detemir was not strictly enforced, with a mean end of trial dose of 0.51 IU/kg per day at the lower end of the 0.4 to 0.9 IU/kg range of other detemir trials, so the comparator was probably undertitrated; sulfonylurea doses were also halved at baseline and then changed differently in the two arms (80 per cent of exenatide patients reduced against 70 per cent of detemir patients). d3 some_concerns: 19 of 111 and 12 of 105 did not complete, the imbalance in reasons is marked (adverse event 12 against 5, withdrawal by subject 1 against 6), and the analyses use last observation carried forward or available data. d4 low: central laboratory assays and standard pressure measurement. d5 low: the sponsor posted the registry results, which match the article's reported direction and significance, and the markers extracted here are all pre-specified secondary outcomes

doubts: every number is from the sponsor's registry record rather than the article, because the article's Table 1 is a graphic behind a subscriber gate; the two sources differ by 0.02 percentage points on HbA1c because of different analysis sets

hsCRP and adiponectin for 216 patients are reported in the article (hsCRP as a geometric mean ratio, significantly better with exenatide, P < 0.004) but their values exist only inside that graphic, so the group's most valuable rows are still missing
fasting glucose, both pressures, total cholesterol and triglycerides have no posted baseline, so five of the six rows stay on the absolute scale and contribute nothing to the percent scale pools
the comparator was probably undertitrated, which flatters the exenatide contrast on glycaemic markers
